intended_object: The unique (empty) proper coloring of a graph on an empty vertex set with colors from any type α. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `Colorable.of_isEmpty`.
explanation: `G.Coloring α` is a graph homomorphism `G →g ⊤` into the complete graph on α. When `V` is empty, the empty function `isEmptyElim` is the only map V → α, and the condition that adjacent vertices get different colors holds vacuously, which is what `isEmptyElim v` proves. The definition is general: any vertex type `V` with `[IsEmpty V]`, any graph `G` and any color type `α`, including an empty one. Because `V` is empty, `G` can only be the empty graph, so the definition is exactly the coloring of an empty graph that the docstring describes. It is used to show that the empty graph is `n`-colorable for every `n`, including `n = 0`. I found no other Mathlib declaration that defines this coloring.
